question: The European Water Resilience Strategy aims to reduce leaks and modernise infrastructure. Under Article 4(3) of Directive 2020/2184 water leakage levels must be assessed and the results notified to the Commission by 12 January 2026. For the Greek islands, we need to know how much water is being lost and prioritise repairing the networks.
Small-scale suppliers also require technical assistance so that they can prepare and implement projects with the help of funding. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Did Greece submit the assessment within the deadline? What are the results for the suppliers covered in the assessment, especially those who supply islands?
What Eu-funded projects are being implemented on the Greek islands to reduce leakages, what is the budget and what are the specific water saving targets?
How will it help small island suppliers record water loss and prepare investor-ready projects, even when they do not fulfil the Directive’s minimum requirements for mandatory assessment?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) In 2026, the Commission received all Member States’ assessments of national water leakage levels, including Greece. Under Article 4(3) of the Drinking Water Directive1, it will use these results to set a leakage threshold by delegated act by 12 January 2028.

As the data do not identify individual water suppliers or supply zones, more detailed information should be requested from the competent Greek authorities. Under Cohesion Policy 2021–20272, regional programmes for the North Aegean, South Aegean and Ionian Islands are investing EUR 96.6 million, including EUR 69.9 million in EU support, to modernise drinking-water networks and reduce leakages.

Around 40%3 of this funding has been selected so far, and at least 251 697 residents are expected to benefit4. The national Environment and Climate Change Programme has launched a EUR 20 million call5 to support drinking-water investments in 39 islands, benefiting 39 856 residents and aiming to reduce network losses below 20%6.

The Commission invites the Honourable Member to contact the competent Greek authorities for detailed information on individual projects under shared management. Cohesion Policy provides support to strengthen the capacity of water service providers through the 2021-2027 Technical Assistance programme7.

The EUR 68 million administrative capacity building roadmap8 lays down a decentralised mechanism providing on-site expert support in three sectors9, including for the preparation and implementation of projects, masterplans, and strategies. Additional technical assistance for beneficiaries is available under the aforementioned programmes.
Islands’ water challenges are recognised and are also central to the EU Strategy for Islands10.
1 Directive (EU) 2020/2184 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2020 on the quality

of water intended for human consumption (recast), OJ L 435, 23.12.2020, p. 1–62. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/2021-2027_en. 3 Cohesion open data platform (https://cohesiondata.ec.europa.eu/2021-2027/2021-2027-Finances-DetailedPlanned-vs-Implemented/3git-md5z/about_data). 4 System for Fund Management in the European Union - SFC2021 data. 5 Under the GR-Eco Islands initiative: https://clean-energy-islands.ec.

9 Water, solid waste, and integrated territorial investments. 10 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions EU strategy for islands, COM52026) 520 final.
